title: Redux Saga
description: Learn complex async patterns with Redux Saga.

data.text: **Redux Saga** is a middleware library that handles complex asynchronous operations using **generator functions** and declarative **effects**. It's more powerful than thunks for handling intricate async flows like parallel execution, task cancellation, and complex event coordination.

While thunks work well for simple async, sagas excel at complex scenarios: waiting for multiple actions, canceling ongoing tasks, handling polling, orchestrating parallel API calls, and testing. Sagas are also easier to test because effects are plain objects.

data.text: Sagas use **generator functions** (functions with `*` and `yield`). Generators can pause execution and resume, making async code look synchronous. Each `yield` produces an effect that the saga middleware executes.

cards.title: Redux Thunk
cards.content: Simple: return functions. Good for basic async. Testing requires mocking. Direct access to dispatch and getState.

cards.title: Redux Saga
cards.content: Declarative effects. Powerful for complex flows. Easier to test (effects are plain objects). Steeper learning curve.

data.title: Complex Saga Patterns
Performance Consideration
data.text: takeEvery runs a saga for every matching action. For scenarios where you only want the latest (like search), use takeLatest to avoid processing stale results.

Build a Real-Time Polling System
data.description: Create a saga-based polling system that fetches data at regular intervals, handles errors gracefully, and can be started/stopped dynamically.

data.title: Saga Testing
Key Takeaways
points: Sagas use generator functions and declarative effects for async operations
Watcher sagas detect actions, worker sagas perform work
Effects (call, put, select) are plain objects, making testing easier
takeEvery runs for every action, takeLatest cancels previous
Choose Saga for complex flows; thunks are simpler for basic async
data.takeaway: Redux Saga provides a powerful model for handling complex async workflows through declarative generator-based effects.
